content:
It is understood that this operation was a joint action by Customs and national security police. Earlier, Customs discovered books with seditious intent in a shipment of goods sent to Hong Kong, and today they searched two bookstores.

It is understood that Leave Bookstore (留下書舍), which announced yesterday (the 14th) that it would close down at 8:30 pm, had police visit to investigate this morning (the 15th). The windows of Leave Bookstore had their blinds pulled down in the afternoon. When staff from a publishing house went to the building to deliver books, they had their identification documents checked and were later allowed to leave.

At around 5:50 pm, police escorted a female shop assistant onto a police vehicle. The shop assistant was dressed in black, with the words "I am a bookstore clerk" written on her clothes, and she was handcuffed and taken away. After the police operation ended, the movie posters outside the bookstore remained, and the bookstore was locked with an iron gate. The poster outside the door bore the words "Live sincerely and uprightly." A towel with the words "Freedom" on one side and "Wind and Rain" on the other that had been hanging at the bookstore window was removed.

Another independent bookstore, Garden Bookstore (田園書屋), was also reportedly searched by police. At around 4:30 pm, police took away one person, along with four blue plastic crates and a black suitcase.

At around 1 pm today, several plainclothes police officers went to Leave Bookstore in Prince Edward to conduct a search. During the operation, plainclothes police officers were seen carrying blue plastic crates upstairs. About two hours later, police put on vests printed with "police." Staff from a publishing house delivering goods upstairs were searched by police and were later allowed to leave. In the afternoon, members of the public occasionally went upstairs to get haircuts or go to work, passing through as usual without being stopped and searched by police.

Leave Bookstore, which opened in 2022, was founded by veteran journalist Sham Wan-wah (岑蘊華) and several former journalists. It focused on books related to news topics and also held reader sharing sessions and other events. In recent months, national security police had successively taken arrest actions against bookstores including One Bookstore (一拳書館) and Hunter Bookstore (獵人書店). Leave Bookstore yesterday issued a closure notice on social media, stating that recent developments may have been the last straw on the camel's back, with the elusive red line also being a reason for closure. They said in a statement that the Secretary had previously made it clear that no explanation would be given as to what books cannot be sold, and that the bookstore had "no ability to judge which books are 'problematic'."

This year, independent bookstores have successively become entangled in national security cases, and some independent bookstores have had their参展資格 (exhibition qualifications) cancelled by the HKTDC (Trade and Industry Department). In March this year, the person in charge of One Bookstore, Pong Yat-ming (龐一鳴), and three staff were arrested by national security police. The four were accused of "selling publications with seditious intent with knowledge," an offence under Article 23, and books including "The Biography of Jimmy Lai" were seized from the bookstore. Pong Yat-ming had earlier been charged under the Education Ordinance for organizing Spanish interest classes at the bookstore, and was fined HK$32,000. A stand-up comedy stage performance held last June led to charges of "operating an unlicensed place of public entertainment" in violation of the Places of Public Entertainment Ordinance, with him and his company each fined HK$3,000, totaling HK$6,000 in fines.

On June 29 this year, the founder of Hunter Bookstore, Wong Man-huen (黃文萱), and her husband were arrested by national security police on suspicion of "committing acts with seditious intent out of seditious intent," an offence under Article 23, and on suspicion of money laundering and other charges. A few days later, news came that Yiu Lam Bookstore (榆林書店) and Lok Man Bookstore (樂文書店) were suddenly disqualified (DQ) by the HKTDC from participating in the Hong Kong Book Fair. The book fair at the Convention and Exhibition Centre (會展) is an important source of annual income for independent bookstores. It is understood that the bookstores had also prepared large quantities of books, and after being suddenly disqualified by the HKTDC, both bookstores had to discount their stock. Yiu Lam Bookstore announced last week that it would "gloriously end its physical store" when its lease expires in April next year.
